_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Before you formed us, you knew us; from the womb you have been our rock.
In you, O Lord, we take refuge.
A woman bent for eighteen years stood up straight at the word of Jesus.
He has loosed our bonds; we stand and praise.
We have come to a kingdom that cannot be shaken.
Let us give thanks, and worship with reverence and awe.
Come, you who were bent low, and lift your heads.
We stand up straight to praise the Lord. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: For eighteen years a woman could not lift her head — bent toward the ground, seeing only feet and dust, until Jesus saw her across the room.
We stand up straight to praise you.
He called her over, laid his hands on her, and something long-locked let go; her spine unfolded and she looked him in the face.
We stand up straight to praise you.
This is the God who knew you before you were formed, who has been your rock since your mother's arms — your refuge, never shaken.
We stand up straight to praise you.
So whatever has bent you low this week, bring it here. The Lord is still setting daughters and sons of Abraham free.
We stand up straight to praise you. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Bent low for years, she stood at his word.
We stand up straight to praise you.
Before we were formed, you knew us and held us.
We stand up straight to praise you.
You are our rock and our unshaken kingdom.
We stand up straight to praise you.
Come, you who were bent low, and lift your heads.
We stand up straight to praise you. Amen.
